problem: The sentence 'The peak stress in the block is 0.446fck' contradicts the block just defined. The equivalent rectangular block has a uniform stress of 0.36fck — it has no peak. The value 0.446fck (= 0.67fck/1.5) is the peak of the real curved (parabolic-rectangular) distribution at the extreme compression fibre, before it is replaced by the equivalent block. As written, a student will think the code block varies from 0.446fck to 0.36fck.
fix: Replace with: 'The equivalent block is uniform at 0.36fck. The real curved distribution that it replaces has its peak 0.446fck (= 0.67fck/1.5) at the extreme compression fibre, and this shape is what fixes the centroid at 0.42xu.'

problem: The chapter says the stress is the average 0.36fck 'over the whole depth xu' and also that C acts at 0.42xu from the top. A uniform stress over xu would put the resultant at 0.5xu. Students notice the mismatch and lose confidence in the model.
fix: Add one sentence: the 0.36fck is the average intensity taken over the compression zone, while the 0.42xu position of the resultant is fixed by the real curved shape; both numbers together are the code's idealisation, not two independent facts about a uniform stress.

problem: The starting line gives xu = 0.48d with no reason, and the answers carry meaningless precision (Ast = 1238.388 mm², Mu = 160.641 kNm). A student cannot tell whether 0.48 is a code limit or an arbitrary choice.
fix: State that 0.48 is the limiting value of xu/d for Fe415 steel, so the section is at Mu,lim. Round the answers to Ast = 1238 mm² (about 1240 mm², say 4 bars of 20 mm) and Mu = 160.6 kNm.

problem: 'Using 0.446fck as the average stress in C = 0.36fck b xu' reads as if the student substitutes into the 0.36 formula; the actual mistake being described is writing the force as 0.446fck b xu.
fix: Rewrite: 'Writing C = 0.446fck b xu, that is, using the peak stress over the full depth xu, overestimates compression; 0.446fck is only the peak of the real distribution, not its average.'
